children: The UK must abandon its planned 2030 ban on new petrol and diesel cars if it wants access to the EU's flagship industrial programme,

. Provost said Britain would need to align with Brussels on tariffs for Chinese imports to join the "Made in Europe" scheme, formally the Industrial Accelerator Act, which currently excludes UK carmakers. He described the UK's combustion‑engine ban as "stupid", arguing there was "no good date" for mandating 100% electric sales.
Ministers are frustrated that the Welsh Government is obstructing a US‑backed space defence radar project in Pembrokeshire,

reported. Plaid Cymru was said to oppose the installation on ideological grounds, with one Labour source claiming the party views the US as an "enemy". The impasse threatens progress on a joint defence initiative signed by the UK, US and Australia, and comes amid strained transatlantic relations after the US withdrew bomber jets from RAF Fairford last month over security concerns.
Andy Burnham's pledge to bring water companies under greater public control could deepen the sector's financial troubles, Moody's has warned, according to

. The ratings agency said persistent political scrutiny and uncertainty over future ownership were undermining investor confidence and raising the cost of capital needed for major upgrades. It cautioned that the Prime Minister's stance - short of full nationalisation but still signalling stronger state involvement - risks another sector‑wide downgrade and delays to essential reform.

The NHS faces a tougher‑than‑usual winter, health secretary Yvette Cooper has warned, as she announced £140m of extra funding for urgent care, The Guardian reported. The money will support 14 projects across England, including new urgent‑care centres, ambulance fleet expansions and emergency‑department upgrades. Cooper said the service had been preparing since July after an exceptionally heavy summer, with 7.3m A&E attendances between June and August - the highest on record for the period.
Israeli settler militants assaulted European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of Cambrai during an olive‑harvesting visit to Taybeh in the occupied West Bank, injuring three people,

reported. Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye‑Aymeries, was knocked to the ground while entering a diplomatic vehicle. His wife and Archbishop Vincent Dollmann were also threatened by a group of masked men, some carrying clubs. The attackers had earlier assaulted Palestinian harvesters, including a woman in her 70s, and smashed the window of a Belgian diplomatic vehicle.
